instructions: Peel the carrots and grate them on the fine holes of a box grater, or in a food processor with the grating disc. Set them aside.
Juice the lemon. In a large bowl, whisk 1 tbsp of the juice with the Dijon, vegetable oil, olive oil, salt and pepper until it thickens slightly. Keep the rest of the juice for the end.
Chop 2 tbsp of the parsley and thinly slice the green onions. Add them to the bowl with the carrots and toss well.
Taste it and add a little more lemon juice or salt if it needs it. Let it sit for 15 minutes before serving so the flavors come together.
Serve cold or at room temperature. For packed lunches, keep it in a covered container in the fridge for up to 3 days, and toss it again before eating.
method_notes: Once Upon a Chef (4.84 from 166 ratings) is the lead: fine shreds of carrot in a lemon and Dijon vinaigrette with parsley and green onion, resting 15 to 30 minutes. It keeps up to 3 days in the fridge, and the carrots soften as they sit. The lead's 1 to 2 tsp of honey is left out to keep this vegan, and the dressing does not need it. David Lebovitz and Pardon Your French make the same salad with a little less oil and add raisins or nuts.
